_comment: OUTPAINTING - extend an image beyond its original frame. FLUX.1 Fill with the OneReward transformer. Takes a 1024x1024 square and grows it into a 2048x1024 cinematic wide, inventing the new left and right thirds so they match the original's light, lens and grain.
_notes: `ImagePadForOutpaint` outputs BOTH the padded image and the mask of the new area, in one node. You do not paint a mask - the padding amounts define it. left/top/right/bottom are pixels of new canvas.

`feathering` (40 here) softens the seam between original and invented pixels. Too low and you get a visible vertical join; too high and the model starts repainting parts of your original. 24-48 is the usable band.

There is NO negative prompt. `ConditioningZeroOut` (node 8) manufactures an empty negative from the positive - that is the Flux convention, and cfg stays at 1.0 because guidance is carried by `FluxGuidance` instead. Setting cfg above 1.0 here produces burnt, oversaturated output.
`FluxGuidance` at **30** looks absurd next to the 4.0 used for FLUX.2 text-to-image, and it is correct - the Fill model is trained at that range. Do not normalise it to match your other Flux graphs.
`DifferentialDiffusion` (node 4) is what makes the feathered mask work as a soft gradient rather than a hard binary. Without it the feathering is ignored and you get a hard seam.

`noise_mask: false` on InpaintModelConditioning for OUTPAINTING - you want the model to see the whole canvas. Set it `true` for object REMOVAL, where you want the masked region genuinely resampled (see workflow 29).

Prompt for the SCENE, not for the edit. 'Remove the frame edge' means nothing; describe what should exist in the widened frame. Keeping it short and consistent with the original's content works better than a long re-description.
This is the OneReward fp8 transformer, deliberately chosen over plain `flux1-fill-dev`: half the size (11 GB vs 22 GB), newer method, and better at removal. Same graph serves both jobs.

inputs.text: An apiary on an overcast morning. More wooden beehive boxes stacked on rough grass, a weathered fence line and pale flat sky continuing to both sides. Soft directionless daylight, muted natural colour, medium format film grain.
